correctness.rationale: Independent replay /workspace/branches/replay_1.py, run with python3, directly summed crossing indicators over the 48 unordered edges of each graph on each of 65,536 binary profiles; it imports no source code and uses neither the supplied row-mask nor edge-increment recurrence. It checked all subset-size totals, every coefficient difference (35 nonzero, all others zero), and the degree and common-neighbor conditions. The latter give A²=4I+2J_16 and the shared spectrum 6,2^(6),−2^(9); the unequal counts of K4 subgraphs (8 vs. 0) certify nonisomorphism. After dividing the parenthetical factor by z^4 the sign is that of g(s)=s²−4q⁶s+6q⁸−2 on s≥2. For q≠1, g(2)=2(q²−1)²(3q⁴+2q²+1)>0; for q<1 the vertex lies left of 2, and for q>1 it lies right of 2 with negative value −2(q⁴−1)²(2q⁴+1). This gives exactly the stated strict intervals; q=1 makes the full difference zero. In the Ising normalization the common prefactor is exp(−48βJ+16βh), q=exp(2βJ), z=exp(−2βh); s=2cosh(4βh) sweeps [2,∞) strictly monotonically for h≥0. Rationalizing the smaller root gives s_−∼(3/2)q², while s_+∼4q⁶, proving the two limits J and 3J at fixed J>0. Spin reversal gives the negative-field comparisons. The uploaded finite certificate was inspected, not executed; the independent replay covers only these two labeled finite graphs.

value.rationale: The rook–Shrikhande pair is a natural fixed spectral indistinguishability test, and the field-resolved Ising partition function is motivated independently of the enumeration. The exact factorization shows that turning on field can reverse, then restore, the strict all-coupling zero-field ordering at every positive temperature. That precise behavior is not a routine corollary of nonisomorphism, graph spectra, or the pair's ground-state thresholds. The crossing is a finite-system comparison, not a claim of a thermodynamic singularity.
